requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs on node1 as a systemd-managed service
requirements.summary: Unit file created with Restart=always, enabled via systemctl enable --now, MainPID confirmed active, and later confirmed enabled/auto-started after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service is configured so the kernel OOM killer will not select it
requirements.summary: OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 set in the unit and verified live via systemctl show and /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj (=-1000), persisting after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Under an actual system-wide OOM condition, the kernel kills the memory-hog process (not inventory-api), and inventory-api keeps serving
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline captured, swap disabled and a hog process driven to ~1.8GB RSS exhausted available memory (13Mi available), dmesg shows the kernel oom-killer selecting and killing pid 1721 (the hog), and the same command shows inventory-api still active and /healthz responding immediately afterward.

requirements.requirement: After the OOM event, hog is gone, inventory-api is unaffected (same PID, correct data), and environment is restored
requirements.summary: MainPID unchanged at 1602, /inventory returns correct JSON, no hog process remains, swap restored to 2GiB/0-used baseline, temp hog files removed.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 55595e92... with active/enabled service and correct curl responses captured; reboot acknowledged asynchronously with a subsequent timeout confirming disconnection; post-restart boot_id a3b4838e... (different) with reset uptime; inventory-api auto-started with new MainPID, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact, correct data, swap at baseline. Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and show no failed services.

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-api as a systemd service with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, then directly demonstrated the required behavior: it induced a genuine system-wide OOM by disabling swap and running a memory hog, and dmesg confirms the kernel killed the hog process while inventory-api remained active and serving, with data and service state verified intact afterward and the environment restored. The separate node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly, with distinct pre/post boot IDs and confirmed service recovery. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence; hygiene is good with only a trivial leftover log file and a well-justified transient oom_score_adj adjustment to protect the exec channel.
limitations: The killed hog process is shown with oom_score_adj:-500 rather than 0, indicating it inherited the protective adjustment intended for the exec/socat management path (since it was spawned from that same session); this did not affect the outcome since inventory-api's -1000 remained more protective, but it means the hog was not tested at a neutral/default oom_score_adj.

No numeric oom_score reading for inventory-api at the moment of the kill was captured beyond the pre-event baseline of 0, though this is not required to confirm the outcome given the direct dmesg kill evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were purposeful and mostly reverted: swapoff/swapon was reversible and restored (cmd-fc8015e6eb1443aa, cmd-579ee791ec9c41d5); the memory-hog script and its logs were removed after the test (cmd-ac91453d0d54422e). The oom_score_adj=-500 tweaks applied to socat/sshd (cmd-fc6cf2e5197d4c5d) to protect the exec/management channel during the induced OOM were a reasonable, low-risk safeguard tied to preserving evidence collection, though not explicitly reset before reboot (they are transient /proc values that reset naturally on reboot, so no lasting residue). One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log created by the reboot wrapper was left behind post-reboot per the after-executor temp-files snapshot, a trivial unreverted artifact. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no unsafe new exposure beyond the intended inventory-api listener on 8080.
